title: Addition of Vectors â€” Same and Opposite Directions
notes: **Case 1 â€” same direction**: let $\vec{P}$ and $\vec{Q}$ act in the same direction. Their sum (resultant) is $\vec{R} = \vec{P} + \vec{Q}$; $\vec{R}$ is also called the resultant vector, drawn head-to-tail.
**Case 2 â€” opposite direction**: let $\vec{P}$ and $\vec{Q}$ act in opposite directions. The resultant is $\vec{R} = \vec{P} + (-\vec{Q}) = \vec{P} - \vec{Q}$, acting along the larger vector.

**Statement**: When two non-zero vectors are represented by two sides of a triangle taken in the same order, their resultant is represented by the third side of the triangle taken in the opposite order.

**Setup**: Let $\vec{P}$ and $\vec{Q}$ act at a point, represented by sides $AB$ and $BC$ of triangle $ABC$ (i.e. $\vec{AB}=\vec{P}$, $\vec{BC}=\vec{Q}$), with resultant $\vec{AC}=\vec{R}$. Let $\theta$ be the angle between $\vec{P}$ and $\vec{Q}$. Draw $CD$ perpendicular to line $AB$ extended.
In right triangle $BCD$: $CD = BC\sin\theta = Q\sin\theta$, and $BD = BC\cos\theta = Q\cos\theta$.
In right triangle $ACD$: $AC^2 = AD^2 + DC^2 = (AB+BD)^2 + DC^2$.
Expanding: $R^2 = P^2 + 2P(Q\cos\theta) + Q^2\cos^2\theta + Q^2\sin^2\theta = P^2 + Q^2 + 2PQ\cos\theta$ (using $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$).
**Magnitude of resultant**: $R = \sqrt{P^2+Q^2+2PQ\cos\theta}$.

**Direction**: in right triangle $ADC$, $\tan\alpha = \dfrac{DC}{AD} = \dfrac{Q\sin\theta}{P+Q\cos\theta}$, so $\alpha = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{Q\sin\theta}{P+Q\cos\theta}\right)$, where $\alpha$ is the angle the resultant makes with $\vec{P}$.

**Special cases**: (i) $\theta=0Â°$ â†’ $R=P+Q$ (maximum), $\alpha=0$. (ii) $\theta=90Â°$ â†’ $R=\sqrt{P^2+Q^2}$, $\tan\alpha=Q/P$. (iii) $\theta=180Â°$ â†’ $R=P-Q$ (minimum), resultant acts along the larger vector.

**Statement**: If two vectors acting at a point are represented in magnitude and direction by the two adjacent sides of a parallelogram drawn from that point, their resultant is represented in magnitude and direction by the diagonal of the parallelogram passing through the same point.

**Derivation**: consider $\vec{P}$ and $\vec{Q}$ inclined at angle $\theta$, forming adjacent sides $AB$ and $AD$ of parallelogram $ABCD$. Draw $CE$ perpendicular to $AB$ extended. In right triangle $BCE$: $CE=Q\sin\theta$, $BE=Q\cos\theta$, so $AE = AB+BE = P+Q\cos\theta$.
In right triangle $ACE$: $AC^2=AE^2+CE^2 \Rightarrow R^2=(P+Q\cos\theta)^2+(Q\sin\theta)^2 = P^2+Q^2+2PQ\cos\theta$.

**Magnitude**: $R=\sqrt{P^2+Q^2+2PQ\cos\theta}$. **Direction**: $\tan\alpha=\dfrac{Q\sin\theta}{P+Q\cos\theta}$ â€” identical results to the triangle law, since the diagonal of the parallelogram is exactly the third side of the triangle formed by $\vec P$ and $\vec Q$.
**Special cases**: (i) $\theta=0Â°$: $R=P+Q$. (ii) $\theta=90Â°$: $R=\sqrt{P^2+Q^2}$. (iii) $\theta=180Â°$: $R=P-Q$.

**Statement**: If a number of vectors are represented in magnitude and direction by the sides of a polygon taken in the same order (head-to-tail), their resultant is represented in magnitude and direction by the closing side of the polygon taken in the opposite order.

**Derivation**: applying the triangle law repeatedly to vectors $\vec{A_1},\vec{A_2},\dots,\vec{A_n}$ placed head-to-tail: $\vec{OB}=\vec{A_1}+\vec{A_2}$, then $\vec{OC}=\vec{OB}+\vec{A_3}=\vec{A_1}+\vec{A_2}+\vec{A_3}$, and so on, until the resultant is $\vec{R}=\vec{A_1}+\vec{A_2}+\vec{A_3}+\cdots+\vec{A_n}$, represented by the vector closing the polygon back to the starting point.

**Q. If two vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ have equal magnitudes $P$ (i.e. $|\vec{A}|=|\vec{B}|=P$), find the magnitude and direction of their resultant.** This is the triangle/parallelogram law with $P=Q$: $R=\sqrt{P^2+P^2+2P^2\cos\theta}=\sqrt{2P^2(1+\cos\theta)}=2P\cos(\theta/2)$, and the resultant bisects the angle between them, $\alpha=\theta/2$.
**Definition**: splitting (breaking) a vector into its different constituent parts is known as resolution of a vector.
If a vector is resolved along two mutually perpendicular directions, it is called **rectangular (perpendicular) resolution**: $R_x=R\cos\theta$ and $R_y=R\sin\theta$.

**Derivation**: let $\vec{R}$ act at a point making angle $\theta$ with the x-axis. Complete parallelogram $OACB$ with $OA$ along the x-axis and $OC$ along the y-axis. By the law of triangle, $\vec{OA}+\vec{OC}=\vec{OD}$, i.e. $\vec{R_x}+\vec{R_y}=\vec{R}$, so $\vec{R}=R_x\hat{i}+R_y\hat{j}$.
In right triangle $OAB$: $\cos\theta=OA/AB \Rightarrow OA=AB\cos\theta \Rightarrow R_x=R\cos\theta$. Also $\sin\theta=OC/OB \Rightarrow R_y=R\sin\theta$.
Combining: **magnitude** $R=\sqrt{R_x^2+R_y^2}$, **direction** $\tan\theta=R_y/R_x$.

**Fig(i): a force of 10 N acts at 30Â° from the y-axis.** Taking components along y and x: $F_y=F\cos30Â°=10\times(\sqrt3/2)=5\sqrt3\,\text{N}\approx8.66\,\text{N}$, $F_x=F\sin30Â°=10\times0.5=5\,\text{N}$.

**Fig(ii): a force of 10 N acts at 45Â° from the y-axis.** $F_x=F\cos45Â°=10\times(1/\sqrt2)=5\sqrt2\,\text{N}\approx7.07\,\text{N}$, $F_y=F\sin45Â°=5\sqrt2\,\text{N}\approx7.07\,\text{N}$ (here $\sin45Â°=\cos45Â°$, so both components come out equal).
**Like (parallel) vectors**: vectors having the same direction, regardless of magnitude.
**Unlike (anti-parallel) vectors**: vectors having opposite directions.
**Co-planar vectors**: vectors that lie in the same plane.
**Null (zero) vector**: a vector with zero magnitude, $\vec{R}=0$. Its direction is indeterminate.

**Unit vector**: a vector having unit magnitude (1) but retaining a direction; used to denote direction only. Denoted with a cap/hat overhead, e.g. $\hat{A}$. Along the x, y, z axes the standard unit vectors are $\hat{i}, \hat{j}, \hat{k}$.

**Definition**: if $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are two vectors, their scalar product (dot product) is $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=ab\cos\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between them. The result is a scalar, e.g. $c=\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=ab\cos\theta$.
**Case 1 â€” perpendicular vectors**: if $\theta=90Â°$, $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=ab\cos90Â°=0$. This is the condition for two vectors to be perpendicular.
**Case 2 â€” parallel vectors**: if $\theta=0Â°$, $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=ab\cos0Â°=ab$. This is the condition for two vectors to be parallel.
**Case 3 â€” anti-parallel vectors**: if $\theta=180Â°$, $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=ab\cos180Â°=-ab$. This is the condition for two vectors to be anti-parallel.

**Dot products of unit vectors**: since the angle between a unit vector and itself is 0Â°: $\hat{i}\cdot\hat{i}=\hat{j}\cdot\hat{j}=\hat{k}\cdot\hat{k}=1$. Since $\hat{i},\hat{j},\hat{k}$ are mutually perpendicular (90Â°): $\hat{i}\cdot\hat{j}=\hat{j}\cdot\hat{k}=\hat{k}\cdot\hat{i}=0$.

**Component-form derivation**: for $\vec{A}=A_1\hat{i}+A_2\hat{j}+A_3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{B}=B_1\hat{i}+B_2\hat{j}+B_3\hat{k}$, expanding $\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B}$ term by term and using the unit-vector dot products above gives $\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B}=A_1B_1+A_2B_2+A_3B_3$.

**Definition**: if $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ are two vectors inclined at angle $\theta$, their vector product (cross product) is $\vec{A}\times\vec{B}=AB\sin\theta\,\hat{n}$, where $\hat{n}$ is a unit vector perpendicular to the plane containing $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$, with direction given by the right-hand rule. The result is a vector: $\vec{C}=\vec{A}\times\vec{B}$.
**Case 1 â€” parallel vectors**: if $\theta=0Â°$, $\vec{A}\times\vec{B}=0$. This is the condition for two vectors to be parallel.
**Case 2 â€” perpendicular vectors**: if $\theta=90Â°$, $|\vec{A}\times\vec{B}|=AB$ (maximum). This is the condition for two vectors to be perpendicular.

**Non-commutative property**: $\vec{A}\times\vec{B} = -(\vec{B}\times\vec{A})$, i.e. reversing the order reverses the direction of the resultant vector (cross product does NOT commute, unlike the dot product).

**Cross products of unit vectors**: $\hat{i}\times\hat{i}=\hat{j}\times\hat{j}=\hat{k}\times\hat{k}=0$ (parallel to themselves). For the mutually perpendicular set (right-hand rule, cyclic order $i\to j\to k\to i$): $\hat{i}\times\hat{j}=\hat{k}$, $\hat{j}\times\hat{k}=\hat{i}$, $\hat{k}\times\hat{i}=\hat{j}$; and reversing order flips sign: $\hat{j}\times\hat{i}=-\hat{k}$, $\hat{k}\times\hat{j}=-\hat{i}$, $\hat{i}\times\hat{k}=-\hat{j}$.

**Q1. Two forces, 10 N acting at 30Â° above the +x-axis and 5 N acting at 45Â° below the +x-axis, act at a point. Find the resultant.** $F_x = 10\cos30Â° + 5\cos45Â° = 8.66+3.54=12.20\,\text{N}$. $F_y = 10\sin30Â° - 5\sin45Â° = 5-3.54=1.46\,\text{N}$ (the second force's y-component is negative since it is below the axis). $F=\sqrt{F_x^2+F_y^2}=\sqrt{12.20^2+1.46^2}\approx12.28\,\text{N}$, at $\theta=\tan^{-1}(1.46/12.20)\approx6.8Â°$ above the x-axis.

**Q2. Two forces, 10 N and 5 N, each act at 30Â° from a common reference line, one above it and one below it. Find the resultant.** $F_x = 10\cos30Â°+5\cos30Â° = (10+5)\times(\sqrt3/2)=7.5\sqrt3\approx12.99\,\text{N}$. $F_y = 10\sin30Â° - 5\sin30Â° = 5-2.5=2.5\,\text{N}$. $F=\sqrt{F_x^2+F_y^2}=\sqrt{12.99^2+2.5^2}\approx13.23\,\text{N}$, at $\theta=\tan^{-1}(2.5/12.99)\approx10.9Â°$ from the reference line, on the side of the larger (10 N) force.

**If two vectors of equal magnitude act perpendicular to each other, find the resultant.** Let $|\vec{A}|=|\vec{B}|=a$ and $\theta=90Â°$. Using $R=\sqrt{A^2+B^2+2AB\cos\theta}=\sqrt{a^2+a^2+2a^2\cos90Â°}=\sqrt{2a^2}=a\sqrt2$. Direction: $\tan\alpha=\dfrac{a\sin90Â°}{a+a\cos90Â°}=\dfrac{a}{a}=1 \Rightarrow \alpha=45Â°$ â€” the resultant bisects the angle between the two equal perpendicular vectors.

**Q. If two equal vectors act perpendicular to each other and their resultant is 1.414 ($\approx\sqrt2$) units, find the magnitude of each vector.** Using $R=a\sqrt2$ from above: $a=\dfrac{R}{\sqrt2}=\dfrac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt2}=1$ unit â€” each vector has magnitude 1 unit.

**If two vectors of equal magnitude 2 m act perpendicular to each other, find the resultant.** Let $|\vec{A}|=|\vec{B}|=2\,\text{m}$, $\theta=90Â°$: $R=\sqrt{A^2+B^2+2AB\cos\theta}=\sqrt{2^2+2^2+0}=\sqrt8=2\sqrt2\,\text{m}$.

Direction: $\tan\alpha=B/A=1 \Rightarrow \alpha=45Â°$, i.e. the resultant lies exactly midway between the two original vectors (e.g. if one points north-of-east and the other south-of-east, the resultant points due east).
